analysis.title: What Does the Power Shortfall Mean for Semis?
key_insights: Morgan Stanley sizes the US data center power shortfall at 57 GW for 2026-28, or 32 GW net of 'time to power' solutions, which is 34% of power demanded.
Nvidia commentary confirms there is not enough power to meet demand and more chips are being built than there are places to put them. MS stays convinced Nvidia has line of sight into chip placement.

MS does not see the power shortfall putting Nvidia and Broadcom 2027 forecasts at risk. Reasons: conservative management guidance, management visibility into chip placement, geographic expansion outside the US, and Nvidia's higher tokens per gigawatt versus peers.
Nvidia and Broadcom have given 12-month outlooks totaling about $800bn of combined AI revenue. MS says this is not at risk today, but the shortfall makes upside harder.
MS sees a risk that ASICs lose share to GPUs in a power-constrained environment, because ASICs produce fewer tokens per watt.

Broadcom guided FY27 AI revenue well above $100bn in March, then guided to $115bn in September. MS says this is less upside than investors expected and may reflect power constraints. The pressure extends to AMD, though warrant arrangements with its largest customers de-risk its estimates.

In a pause, MS expects the most disruption at the tail of the bullwhip, in memory, optics, and small-dollar components such as power management and analog parts that are most likely to be over-ordered.

Customers could push out deliveries or cancel orders for chips that cannot be deployed. MS notes the annual chip cadence and limited power raise the opportunity cost of holding GPUs that cannot be powered up.
Power access is concentrating in large, credit-worthy players. Hyperscalers are getting power faster. Smaller neoclouds without credit backing, non-US players, and ASIC-heavy buyers are at risk.

MS forecasts hyperscalers and neoclouds at 60-95% of global data center capacity additions from 2026-28. It hears Amazon is well positioned on power, and that Google adds the most incremental capacity in 2027-28 and so could face more difficulty securing power.

International expansion will not absorb the US shortfall. MS cut its US share of global compute to 55% from 60%. Europe has limited room, the Middle East carries geopolitical risk, and the Asia team's forecast already assumes 14 GW of US demand spilling into Asia through 2030.

Behind-the-meter (BTM) generation is the main upside driver. MS models 11-49 GW of BTM turbines and engines, with 19 GW in the base case. 11 GW is firm contracted deals and 49 GW is factory capacity. If 30 GW of BTM comes online in 2026-28, the shortfall falls to 21 GW.
Bloom Energy fuel cells are forecast at 6 GW for 2026-28 with possible upside from site expansion. MS calls Bloom a key beneficiary of the time-to-power shortfall.

Labor and politics limit the upside. CSIS estimates the US needs 140K+ more skilled tradespeople by 2030. The existing labor base supports 10-20 GW of annual gas additions, and data center pushback and moratoriums add friction.

MS expects premia and urgency to rise for time-to-power solutions in the US, including BTM generation and repurposing grid access held by former Bitcoin miners, and for data center growth outside the US.
Total shortfall is unchanged. MS raised non-AI data center demand and cut US compute share to 55%, and the two changes offset each other.

market_movers.rationale: MS prefers Nvidia as the power risk grows, citing its broadest geographic and customer footprint and more tokens per watt. Roughly half of its business is outside traditional hyperscalers.
MS is convinced Broadcom can meet its 12-month outlook. The September FY27 AI revenue guide of $115bn showed less upside than investors expected, and ASIC exposure carries power-access risk.
The power shortfall puts some pressure on AMD, but warrant dynamics with its largest customers significantly de-risk estimates.
MS forecasts 6 GW of Bloom Energy fuel cells in 2026-28 with possible upside from site expansion, and calls Bloom a key beneficiary of the time-to-power shortfall.
Memory is flagged as an area of concern in a bear case, where shortage-driven pricing supports revenue and EPS and over-ordering is most likely.
Memory is named as an area of downstream concern if chip deliveries are pushed out or cancelled because of power limits.

sector_views.rationale: 2027 Nvidia and Broadcom numbers are seen as safe. Downstream memory, optics, power management, analog, and ASICs face risk from the power shortfall in a bear case and beyond 2027.
MS is more bullish on hyperscalers because large, credit-worthy players are getting power access faster.
Time-to-power providers, including BTM turbines and Bloom fuel cells, should win lucrative agreements for 2027 and 2028 supply.

earnings_insights: Broadcom guided FY27 AI revenue well above $100bn in March 2026, then to $115bn in its September 2026 guidance. Both are company guidance, not reported results.
Nvidia and Broadcom have given 12-month outlooks totaling about $800bn of combined AI revenue. This is company guidance.

macro_indicators.indicator: US data center power shortfall 2026-28, before time-to-power solutions
macro_indicators.interpretation: Demand for AI data center power exceeds what US supply can deliver, which constrains chip placement.

macro_indicators.indicator: US data center power shortfall 2026-28, net of time-to-power solutions
macro_indicators.interpretation: The midpoint case after probability-weighted BTM turbines, Bloom fuel cells, and nuclear. The range is 32-42 GW, or 34-43%.

macro_indicators.indicator: BTM turbines and engines coming online
macro_indicators.interpretation: Faster BTM builds are the main upside driver to the shortfall call.
Possible upside from reported site expansion.
More compute is shifting abroad, but not enough to absorb the US shortfall.

macro_indicators.indicator: Hyperscaler and neocloud share of global data center capacity additions
macro_indicators.interpretation: Capex is concentrating among a few large players.

crypto_views: Grid access owned by former Bitcoin mining companies is a source of 'time to power' capacity. MS models crypto sites of 2 GW in 2026 rising to 12 GW cumulative by 2028, counted within data centers under construction or turbines.

trade_ideas.description: Prefer Nvidia over ASIC-exposed names in a power-constrained environment
trade_ideas.rationale: Nvidia has the broadest geographic and customer footprint and more tokens per watt of power.
trade_ideas.risk: AI end markets do not materialize as expected, or AMD emerges as a viable GPU competitor.

trade_ideas.description: Own Bloom Energy as a beneficiary of the time-to-power shortfall
trade_ideas.rationale: MS forecasts 6 GW of fuel cells in 2026-28 with possible upside from site expansion.

risk_factors: Chips built but not deployable could lead to delivery push-outs or order cancellations, hitting memory, optics, power management, and analog first.
ASICs may lose share to GPUs because of lower tokens per watt.
Smaller neoclouds, non-US players, and less credit-worthy buyers may fail to secure power.
Labor shortages, permitting, and political pushback limit BTM and gas buildout.
Beyond 2027, the shortfall grows and raises risk across the chip ecosystem.
Middle East expansion carries geopolitical risk.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 shows incremental global data center demand of 32/56/86/124 GW for 2026-2029, less a US power shortfall of 9/5/18/35 GW, with hyperscaler and neocloud share of capacity additions at 94%/64%/57% for 2026-28.
Exhibit 2 shows annual hyperscaler and neocloud capacity additions of 11.0/21.7/32.2/39.0 GW for 2025-2028, led by Google.
Exhibit 4 shows a net shortfall of 42 GW at the low end, 32 GW at the midpoint, and none at the high end, equal to 43%, 34% and 0% of 2026-28 US data center deployments.
Exhibit 5 shows a midpoint net shortfall of 9 GW in 2026, 15 GW in 2027, 32 GW in 2028 and 68 GW in 2029 on a cumulative basis.
geopolitical: An AWS data center was hit by Iran strikes, which MS cites as a reason Middle East expansion is difficult.
Growing political pushback, moratoriums, and public opposition to data centers and AI in the US.

tension_points.bull_case: Nvidia and Broadcom management have line of sight to chip placement, guidance already allows for a land, power and shell shortage, and Nvidia's tokens per watt and global footprint protect its 2027 numbers.
tension_points.bear_case: The US power shortfall worsens beyond 2027, ASICs lose share, and undeployable chips lead to delivery push-outs or cancellations that hit memory, optics, and analog first.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A pause in chip deliveries or order cancellations from customers who cannot power their data centers.

tension_points.bull_case: Firm BTM deals total 11 GW, factory capacity supports up to 49 GW, and manufacturer orders of 25-30 GW could lift annual additions to 15 GW or more from 2028.
tension_points.bear_case: Labor availability, complex engineering, permitting, and political pushback limit how fast BTM comes online.

theme_stances.key_argument: US data center developers face a net 32 GW power shortfall through 2028, and Nvidia commentary confirms it.
theme_stances.evidence: The power shortfall is real and affecting semis

theme_stances.key_argument: ASICs produce fewer tokens per watt, so they risk losing share to GPUs in a power-constrained environment.
theme_stances.evidence: ASICs will lose share in a power-constrained environment relative to GPUs

theme_stances.key_argument: Faster BTM turbine and fuel cell builds are the main upside driver to the shortfall, and time-to-power providers will win lucrative agreements.
theme_stances.evidence: Bloom Energy is a key beneficiary of this "time to power" shortfall
